questions.prompt: Rice A and B cost ₹30 and ₹90 per kg; pulses C and D cost ₹100 and ₹120 per kg. Buy at least 1 kg each of A and B and 0.5 kg each of C and D. Find the minimum and maximum costs of 5 kg.
hints: Allocate every remaining kilogram to the cheapest item for the minimum and the costliest item for the maximum.
questions.solution: The compulsory 3 kg costs $30+90+0.5(100)+0.5(120)=230$. There are 2 kg left. The cheapest choice adds $2(30)=60$, giving ₹290. The costliest adds $2(120)=240$, giving ₹470. Both allocations satisfy every lower bound. Hence **C**.
questions.theory: For a linear cost $\sum c_i x_i$ with $x_i\ge l_i$ and $\sum x_i=W$, write $x_i=l_i+z_i$. Then $z_i\ge0$ and $\sum z_i=R=W-\sum l_i$. The variable cost is a weighted average of the coefficients times $R$, so it lies between $R\min c_i$ and $R\max c_i$. These bounds are attained by putting all excess mass in an extremal item. Check feasibility $W\ge\sum l_i$ first. Upper limits on quantities would require allocating the remainder in price order rather than all to one item.

similar_questions.prompt: Two items cost ₹20 and ₹50/kg. At least 1 kg of each is required; buy 4 kg. Find the cost range.
similar_questions.solution: The compulsory cost is ₹70 and 2 kg remain. The range is ₹110–₹170.
If the cheapest coefficient is unique and positive remainder is available, all remainder must go to that item. Equal cheapest prices give multiple minima.
